title: EXP-016-R2 — Clean Replay: FormSync Script Saved-Form Representation
objective: In a fresh worker execution, use the existing factory-owned User-scope Form FX_FormVariableLab05 and the supported Runtime FormSync Script utility to independently reproduce the EXP-016 saved-Form representation path. Select the intended configuration as Source, explicitly use Filter Configuration=Source, constrain or verify the exact User/ScopeName and Form identity, include exactly the intended scoped Form row, and generate the Script with Output=View. Capture evidence that the generated representation identifies the intended Form and visibly contains the same class of variable-related metadata handling observed in EXP-016. This replay must remain strictly non-mutating and must not interpret generic Variables/FormID handling as proof that any specific Form variable was serialized.

in_scope: Confirm a live supported Mongoose/Web Client session and User editing scope before inspection
Open Runtime FormSync through the supported UI
Select the intended DEM configuration as Source
Filter to Form objects and FX_FormVariableLab05
Select the exact User/ScopeName where the UI permits, or visibly verify the returned row's User/Group Name before inclusion
Refresh the FormSync object list, Deselect All, and include exactly the verified FX_FormVariableLab05 User-scoped row
Use Script with Output=View and Generate
Capture the generated representation showing the target Form identity/scope and variable-related metadata handling
Record browser and repository evidence under evidence/EXP-016-R2/
out_of_scope: Creating, editing, renaming, deleting, or saving any Form or Form variable
Determining whether any specific EXP-014, EXP-015, or FX_FormVariableLab05 variable was serialized
Searching for a controlled variable name/value as positive serialization evidence
Treating absence of a variable name as negative serialization evidence
Troubleshooting or enabling Pseudo Code Generate
Testing cache, unload, IDO metadata, transaction, commit, or physical database durability behavior
Promoting generated SQL table names, columns, numeric scope codes, or statement layout as stable automation contracts
Modifying recipes, AGENTS.md, environment documentation, or unrelated experiment records

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Do not create, edit, rename, delete, Save, Save As, or Regenerate any Mongoose Form or Form variable
Do not execute or preview FX_FormVariableLab05 at runtime
Do not invoke Unload All Global Form Objects, ClearCache, metadata unload, or change User Preferences
Do not invoke FormSync Import, Synchronize, Copy, Delete, or any operation that applies generated SQL to a target database
Do not use direct database queries, internal APIs, reverse-engineered payloads, Ext internal stores, or network payload contents as authoritative saved-definition evidence
Do not claim that generic Variables/FormID SQL proves a specific variable exists or was serialized
Do not log, print, expose, or screenshot credential values
Do not modify any non-FX_ Mongoose artifact
prohibited_patterns: \b(unload all global form objects|clearcache|unload ido metadata)\b

acceptance_checks.description: Before FormSync inspection, evidence proves a live supported Mongoose/Web Client session and User editing scope without exposing credential values.

Evidence proves exactly the intended existing Form is selected using Name=FX_FormVariableLab05 plus ScopeType=User plus the exact ScopeName/User identity; if the User filter is blank or broader than one user, the included grid row's User/Group Name is visibly verified before Inc is selected.
Evidence shows Runtime FormSync configured with the intended configuration as Source and Filter Configuration explicitly set to Source, with the object list narrowed to FX_FormVariableLab05.
After Refresh List and Deselect All, evidence shows exactly one verified scoped FX_FormVariableLab05 row included in the Script batch and no other object included.

Script with Output=View successfully generates a visible representation that identifies FX_FormVariableLab05 and its scoped identity and contains variable-related Forms-database metadata handling of the same semantic class observed in EXP-016; generic metadata handling is explicitly recorded as insufficient to prove any specific variable exists.

A controlled-action audit proves no Form/variable mutation, Save/Save As/Regenerate, runtime execution, cache/global-object/IDO-metadata action, preference change, FormSync Import/Synchronize/Copy/Delete, SQL application, direct database query, or internal API/Ext-store evidence was used.

Final repository audit shows experiment-attributable changes confined to the EXP-016-R2 experiment record and evidence/EXP-016-R2/; no recipe, environment, AGENTS.md, unrelated experiment record, or Mongoose artifact was modified.

initial_instruction: Perform a fresh, strictly read-only replay of the successful final EXP-016 FormSync Script path on the existing User-scoped FX_FormVariableLab05. Confirm live session and User scope first. In Runtime FormSync, select the intended configuration as Source, set Filter Configuration=Source, constrain or visibly verify the exact User/ScopeName and exact Form name, Refresh List, Deselect All, include exactly the verified FX_FormVariableLab05 row, then use Script with Output=View and Generate. Capture evidence of the scoped Form identity and variable-related metadata handling, but do not infer that any specific Form variable was serialized from generic Variables/FormID statements. Do not mutate any Mongoose artifact or perform any cache, preference, runtime, database-apply, internal-API, or direct-SQL action.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261004-094134-Cn9j. Rationale: EXP-016 ultimately established one successful observed FormSync Script path for producing a Forms-database-oriented representation of a selected customized Form, but that path has not been independently replayed. This experiment therefore replays only the representation-generation procedure and does not attempt to resolve EXP-014/EXP-015 variable serialization.
